I have been doing this wheat-maize rotation for many years on this land, so I already know what works. The land here in Quzhou is alright but not rich — if I do not feed it well, the yield drops fast. My son works in the city and sends some money, so I can afford the fertilizer I need, but I still count every bag. I will not waste money, but I also will not cut corners on fertilizer — one bad harvest hurts more than a few extra yuan on urea.

For wheat this winter, I will plant Jimai variety like last year, neighbors got good yield from it. I will put down diammonium phosphate as base fertilizer before sowing — about 2 bags (100 jin, 50 kg) per mu, that gives me the phosphorus and some nitrogen to start. Then in spring at jointing stage I top-dress with urea, one bag per mu (25 kg). I also add some potassium chloride at base, maybe 15 jin per mu. Wheat needs water — I irrigate before winter (dong shui), again at jointing, and once more at grain filling if it is dry. Three times is my habit. For pesticide, I spray herbicide in early spring, then once for aphids and powdery mildew around flowering. Plough with rotary tiller after the maize is cleared.

For maize in summer, I plant hybrid seed (Zhengdan or Denghai) right after wheat harvest, no-tillage direct seeding saves time and diesel. Maize does not need as much as wheat in my experience, but I still give it one bag of compound fertilizer at sowing (25 kg) and top-dress urea at big trumpet stage, one bag per mu. Summer rain usually covers most of it, but I irrigate once at tasseling if dry. Spray once for corn borer, maybe twice if armyworm comes. My maize yields usually over 550 kg per mu, sometimes 600.
